coverage_is_a_floor: ASC 280 requires naming a customer only at >=10% of revenue. This source systematically misses smaller-but-real relationships, most supplier relationships, and every disclosure that says 'Customer A' without naming. An absent edge is NOT evidence of no relationship.
as_of_date_provenance: Each edge's as_of_date is the filing date of the 10-K that disclosed it, satisfying Patch 11 structurally: the relationship was public on that date by construction.

provisional_feature_candidate.decision_point: Phase 2 feature-list lock. Including this is a preregistered decision to be made BEFORE results are seen, not an adoption that happens because the data exists.
provisional_feature_candidate.why_distinct_from_coverage_thinness: coverage/thinness measures ATTENTION paid to a peer (search volume, analyst count, news volume) as a proxy for whether the market already prices a link. This measures how much of the peer's OWN REVENUE depends on its largest customer -- a property of its business, not of attention to it. A thinly-covered peer may have no concentration; a heavily-covered one may have 90%. Merging them would silently redefine the existing proxy.
provisional_feature_candidate.provenance: Each value carries the filing date of the 10-K that disclosed it, so it is point-in-time by construction.
known_limitations: ASC 280 discloses only concentrations at or above ~10% of revenue, so a null is 'nothing above the threshold', never zero.
Aggregate disclosures ('our 10 largest customers') are excluded and contribute nothing to this feature.
Values are as-reported and are not normalised across differing revenue bases or fiscal calendars.
One filing per company (most recent 10-K); this is not a panel.
